chapter: Japan trip, publishing and early influences
title: The Japan tour's pay shortfall and the dummy contract
summary: Gil explains the misunderstanding over expenses, the Japanese limit on taking cash out, the dummy contract, and why he made no money.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: About two weeks I think. I made two albums.........(We had about 25 men, all Japanese... ?).

Well (we had a misunderstanding (I got things wrong?) about that too. I came with two three thousand dollars They were going to pay transportation less than I had planned. It was (a misinterpretation?) I thought, but they didn't think so. ( ... Marvin Peterson ?).
Marvin Peterson is your trumpet player?

Right. It cost roughly a thousand dollars a piece for us you know. Plus a thousand for Anita and a thousand for the children. So that added to the money was five thousand. I expected to get three of that five. The Japanese Government has a rule or a law or whatever you call it, a stipulation that people coming over there to work are not allowed to take more than three thousand dollars in cash out with them when they leave. So I had to sign this dummy contract which had the amount that would be permissible for me to take out.

They considered Anita as my secretary and one or two other items and it worked out like eight thousand or something like that. I assumed the contract was specifically responsible for the transportation because you didn't want to be stuck with people you know, (Unintelligible ?). So I knew (it was within?) our dummy figure but I didn't know the dollar was It didn't work out very well that way. dummy also./ Although we really weren't ( ?). They were all very gracious and everything. We didn't make any money on the trip
because ( ?). And I hadn't had the albums out yet so, there wasn't a big general turn out from the public so (invaluable ?).
They passed out five million hand bills. And they made out some beautiful programs and I'll show them to you too. We Did a lot of nice work. So I couldn't really consider him, you know.
